references.text: David's acknowledgment of submitting to God's will reflects Jesus' prayer that God's will be done, even in the face of suffering.
The prophecy about the Lord's suffering servant who gives his life for many reflects Jesus' acceptance of God's will for salvation.
Luke's account of Jesus' prayer in Gethsemane emphasizes Jesus' surrender to God's will, paralleling Matthew.
Jesus' expression of doing not his own will but the will of the one who sent him mirrors his prayer in Gethsemane.
Jesus' commitment to carrying out the Father's will is a central theme in his prayer in Gethsemane.
The author of Hebrews refers to Psalm 40:8 (in the LXX) as a prediction about Christ, highlighting his willingness to do God's will, paralleling his prayer in Gethsemane.
